what_its_for: Magnesium hydroxide is used to relieve occasional constipation (it helps you have a bowel movement) and to treat heartburn, sour stomach, and acid indigestion. It works as a laxative by drawing water into your intestines to help soften stools, and as an antacid by neutralizing excess stomach acid.
how_to_take: Shake the liquid form well before each use. Take this medicine by mouth with a full 8-ounce glass of water. You can take it with or without food. If you are using it for constipation, drinking extra fluids throughout the day will help it work better. Follow the directions on the package carefully, and do not take more than recommended. This medicine is meant only for short-term use — do not use it for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: The usual laxative dose is 2 to 4 tablespoons (30 to 60 mL) of liquid once daily at bedtime, or as directed. For antacid use, the usual dose is 1 to 3 teaspoons (5 to 15 mL) up to 4 times a day. For children under 12 years, always check the package label or ask your doctor or pharmacist for the right dose based on your child's age and weight. Do not give to children under 2 years old unless directed by a doctor.
missed_dose: Magnesium hydroxide is usually taken only when needed, not on a regular daily schedule. If your doctor has told you to take it regularly and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the liquid. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking magnesium hydroxide within 2 hours of other medicines, especially antibiotics (such as tetracyclines or fluoroquinolones), because it may prevent your other medicines from being absorbed properly. Avoid using this medicine for more than 7 days in a row without talking to your doctor. Do not use if you have stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid excessive use of alcohol while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: no bowel movement within 6 hours of taking a laxative dose, severe stomach pain, cramping, nausea, or vomiting, rectal bleeding or blood in your stool, sudden changes in bowel habits that last more than 2 weeks, signs of too much magnesium in your body such as muscle weakness, slow or irregular heartbeat, feeling very drowsy, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you have kidney disease before using this product, as magnesium can build up to dangerous levels in people with kidney problems.
when_it_works: For constipation, magnesium hydroxide usually causes a bowel movement within 30 minutes to 6 hours after taking it. For heartburn or indigestion, you should feel relief within 5 to 30 minutes of taking it. If your symptoms do not improve or get worse, speak with your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should ask their doctor before using this medicine. People with kidney disease should not use magnesium hydroxide without first talking to their doctor, because the kidneys remove magnesium from the body, and kidney problems can cause dangerous levels of magnesium to build up. Elderly patients may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine and should use it with caution. For children under 12 years old, always consult a doctor or pharmacist for proper dosing guidance.
